event.name: 2026 Taiwan Blues ICU
event.venue: Main Venue and City Social Spaces

home.priorityTitle: The main problem is not the amount of content. It is the order of information.
home.audienceTitle: Different visitors decide whether to join based on different questions.
home.restructureTitle: The site should first work as a clear event entry point, then grow into a fuller festival experience.

hero.title: 2026 Taiwan Blues ICU
hero.subtitle: A Blues dance weekend in Taipei with live music, inspiring teachers, and dancers from around the world.
hero.description: A Blues dance weekend in Taipei with live music, inspiring teachers, and dancers from around the world.
hero.story2: A Blues dance weekend in Taipei with live music, inspiring teachers, and dancers from around the world.

highlights.title: State clearly what kind of event this is
highlights.description: The homepage should set expectations first. This is a Blues dance centered weekend, not a generic social dance party or a loose workshop page.

highlights.title: Put decision-making info early
highlights.description: Visitors care about fit, pass differences, and whether the weekend is worth committing to. That information should not be buried.

highlights.title: Make music and place part of the appeal
highlights.description: If the event is in Taipei, the local atmosphere, night energy, and live music should be part of the story. That is what makes it feel like a festival.

audience.title: People new to Blues
audience.description: They need to know where they can enter and whether the event feels approachable.

audience.title: Experienced social dancers
audience.description: They want a fast read on the teaching quality, music, class depth, and social floor energy.

audience.title: Out-of-town or international visitors
audience.description: They care more about transport, lodging areas, venue flow, and whether the full weekend plan feels smooth.

restructure: The homepage should answer three things first: what this event is, why it is worth attending, and what to do next.
Navigation should use visitor language, not internal category language.
The schedule page should explain the rhythm of the weekend, not only list blocks of time.
The teachers page should explain what each teacher and musician brings, not only show names.
The info page should consolidate FAQ, audience fit, and on-site policies.
Venue and contact should stay separate so first-time visitors can find what they need quickly.

teachers.label: Artists
teachers.title: Teachers & Musicians
teachers.description: This page should clearly present Partner Blues, Solo Blues, and Live Music as three distinct content lines rather than as one long list of names.

partner.title: Partner Blues Teachers
partner.description: Damon Stone and Kelsy Stone should anchor the Partner Blues track, with clear emphasis on class direction such as connection, conversation, and partner musicality.

solo.title: Solo Blues Teacher
solo.description: Catherine Palmier should sit clearly on the solo track so visitors immediately understand that the event includes more than partner classes.

music.title: Live Music
music.description: The Five Box and Stef Rosen should not be treated as small-print details. For a Blues event, musicians are core reasons to attend.

schedule.label: Schedule
schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.description: This page should do more than present a timetable. It should help people understand the rhythm of the weekend and how to plan arrival, classes, social dancing, and departure.

friday.title: Arrive, warm up, and open the social floor
items: Check-in and welcome moments lower the barrier for first-time attendees.
An evening welcome social helps people settle into the music, the floor, and each other.
A short live set or DJ set can establish the musical tone of the weekend.

saturday.title: Main teaching day
items: Daytime workshops should clearly open both the Partner and Solo tracks.
Leave room for breaks and movement between venues so the day does not feel overloaded.
The main party and live band should bring class material directly back onto the social floor.

sunday.title: Close, deepen, and leave with connection
items: Musicality, connection, or culture-focused classes can work well as closing sessions.
A tea dance, community jam, or chill social gives the weekend a more complete landing.
The end time should be clearly shown so out-of-town guests can plan travel.

registration.label: Registration
registration.title: Registration
registration.description: This page should not only present a button. It should help visitors decide which pass fits them, whether they should register now, and where to look when they have questions.
registration.cta: Official registration link goes here later

passes.title: Current pass structure
points: Early Bird Full Pass: offered in Group and Single versions as the main early release option.
Full Pass: the regular full-event pass covering the main classes and parties.
Party Pass: for people mainly coming for social dancing and live music.
Single Day Pass: for people joining one day only, attending for the first time, or still deciding.

levels.title: Make class choice and level questions clear
points: The difference between Group and Single Early Bird Full Pass should be explained clearly.
Clarify whether Partner and Solo classes are selected separately or fully included in the Full Pass.
If there is level placement, explain it directly rather than only saying open level.
Refund, transfer, and waitlist policy should sit close to the registration area.

decision.title: The page should work like a decision page
points: Add a pass comparison table before the registration button so differences are obvious at a glance.
If you have an early bird period, show the exact deadline date.
If domestic and international payments differ, explain that clearly as well.

venue.label: Venue
venue.title: Venue
venue.description: The venue page should help both local and out-of-town visitors quickly understand where the event is, how to get there, and where it is convenient to stay.

main.title: Main venue information
main.description: Add the full address, map, nearest metro station, walking time, and venue photos. If workshops and parties use different spaces, say that directly.

stay.title: Suggested lodging areas
stay.description: Do not only list one hotel. Suggest two or three useful neighborhoods and note travel time.

transport.title: Transport and late-night movement
transport.description: If parties run late, include taxi notes, metro last train details, and nearby convenience spots.

info.label: Info
info.title: Info
info.description: This page should serve as the most practical pre-event page, collecting audience fit, event format, FAQ, and on-site policies in one place.

audience.title: Who this is for
audience.description: State clearly who 2026 Taiwan Blues ICU is for, such as social dancers with prior experience, newcomers to Blues, or dancers wanting both Partner and Solo classes in one weekend.

format.title: Event format
format.description: List workshops, parties, live music, and any special sessions clearly, and keep the framing consistent with the homepage.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.description: It should answer whether beginners can join, whether a fixed partner is needed, how Solo and Partner tracks relate, and how international attendees can pay.

policy.title: On-site policy
policy.description: A code of conduct, safety, and respect policy will make the event feel more mature and more welcoming for first-time attendees.

contact.label: Contact
contact.title: Contact
contact.description: This page should do more than list an email. It should show where registration questions, partnerships, and general inquiries should go.

primary.title: Primary contact
primary.description: At minimum, provide email and Instagram. If registration questions are common, add a short note to route them.

social.title: Social links
social.description: If Instagram or Facebook will carry ongoing updates, show them clearly on this page rather than hiding them only in the footer.

partnership.title: Partnerships and sponsorship
partnership.description: If you expect brand partnerships, photographers, volunteers, or lodging partners, reserve space for that here.

about.label: About
about.title: About
about.description: This page should carry the event vision and positioning rather than repeating the homepage CTA.

vision.title: Event vision
vision.description: This page should answer why you are organizing this event and what you want people to take away from it.

curatorial.title: Curatorial perspective
curatorial.description: If the event values cultural context, musicality, community safety, or local connection, this is where that position should become explicit.

community.title: Community commitment
community.description: You can add a code of conduct and a safety and respect policy here to make the brand feel more grounded and mature.

footer.description: A Blues dance weekend in Taipei with live music, inspiring teachers, and dancers from around the world.
